result: I built the acute:chronic workload ratio (ACWR) feature for the Pitcher Injury Risk pipeline. It divides a 7-day acute load by a 28-day chronic load using a rolling window over each pitcher's pitch counts, excluding the current appearance so the game cannot leak into its own window. I used a time-based train/test split instead of a random one, because pitcher-seasons are time-ordered and a random split leaks future information into training. The ratio is clamped to avoid division by zero when the chronic window has no games. I validated it on synthetic data with three scenarios: a steady workload (ratio near 1.0), a spike (ratio above 1.5), and a first appearance (ratio near 0, confirming no leakage). The implementation reuses the existing rolling-window helper in workload_features.py, which already applies a closed='left' convention so the current game never counts toward its own acute or chronic sum. Tests cover each scenario and the division-by-zero clamp, and the feature adds one column to the existing workload feature pipeline output.
